To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the melanin-contracting hormone producing neurons in hypothalamus are strongly active during paradoxical sleep and that the ICV administration of melanin-contractin hormone increases paradoxical sleep and slow wave sleep.

the melanin-concentration hormone producing neurons are strongly active in the paradoxical sleep, and that intracerebro-ventricular administration of melanin-concentration-hormone increases paradoxical sleep.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role played by melanin-concentating hormone in the regulation of sleep and wakefulness.
the role of melanin concentrating hormone in sleep regulation and narcoleps.
the role of melanin concentrating hormone (MCH)-producing neurons in the central nervous systems of rats, in particular, in relation to paradoxical sleep.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MCH is an endogenous sleep factor.
MCH neurons play a role in the central regulation (i.e. homeostatic) of paradoxical sleep (or REM sleep).
MCH neurons are strongly active in PS, and MCH is a hypnogenic peptide.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MCH is not only involved in the regulation of food intake but also in the regulation of sleep-wake cycle.
MCH neurons are involved in the regulation of sleep-wake cycle, especially PS.
the MCH neurons are activated during PS and that MCH is able to increase the PS and slow wave sleep quantities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MCH neurons are strongly active when paradoxical sleep is enhanced, and that MCH ICV administration increases PS and SWS.
MCH is an important regulator of sleep-wake states.
MCH neurons might have an active role in the regulation of paradoxical (REM) sleep.
